observed_original_abi.calling_convention_caveat: The derived ABI record names __thiscall but lists candidate_conventions [__thiscall, __fastcall] with ambiguities []. For a function of one register argument and zero stack arguments the two conventions emit byte-identical machine code, and no byte of this body separates them. The only convention the bytes ELIMINATE is __cdecl, because 0x00c71e31 copies ECX on entry and a __cdecl receiver would be at [ESP+4]. Whether the register argument is a C++ `this` on a class or an ordinary first parameter is UNKNOWN: receiver.bounds_only is true and class_type, namespace, sdk_type and sdk_name are all null in the live record. The macro in the header is a NAMING of the record's own conclusion, not a discrimination, and no assertion in the package depends on it.
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX, read at 0x00c71e31 (`8b f1`, MOV ESI,ECX) before any definite write; copied into ESI and then read back through ESI at 0x00c71e33, 0x00c71e47 and 0x00c71e50. The record's receiver.shape is R-ALIAS, which is exactly this: the body aliases its receiver into a scratch register rather than dereferencing ECX directly.
observed_original_abi.ret_form: RET (0x00c71e66 and 0x00c71e6a, both the bare 0xc3, no imm16)
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the passing arm returns 0x00ba9370's result verbatim - neither 0x00c71e65 (POP ESI) nor 0x00c71e66 (RET) touches EAX; the null arm returns a full 32-bit zero from `33 c0` at 0x00c71e67
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: MODELLED AS A 32-BIT UNSIGNED DWORD, WITH THE GAME-LEVEL TYPE LEFT UNKNOWN. What the machine proves is exact and narrow: EAX is the return register and a full dword arrives in it on BOTH reachable exits - `33 c0` is XOR EAX,EAX with EAX both sides, not the 8-bit form, so no byte of the null arm's return is undefined - and the passing arm's width is 0x00ba9370's to establish, which its own listing does (its only writes to EAX are `33 c0` and `8b 40 14`, both full 32-bit). The derived record's `register_class: integral` and `type: null` are a single heuristic. The source-level type is NOT decided, because the sampled callers point both ways: 0x00ad4a2f is `85 c0` TEST EAX,EAX + JZ, a NULL TEST that a pointer and an integer share, while 0x00ad4a3f is `8b 80 84 00 00 00` MOV EAX,[EAX+0x84], a DEREFERENCE of the result at +0x84. std::uint32_t is the spelling that is true of both readings and asserts neither. `sret.present: false` is an APPROXIMATION whose own basis warns the absence is weak, and `variadic` is UNKNOWN.
observed_original_abi.locals: none; the body allocates no frame, declares no local and builds no record. `PUSH ESI`/`POP ESI` is the callee-saved register contract for ESI, not a local: 0x00c71e31 WRITES ESI (ModRM 0xf1 is reg=110), and the derived record independently lists saved_registers: [ESI].
observed_original_abi.outgoing_calls: three direct and one indirect. 0x00c71e3d CALL 0x00b8dab0 (the receiver hand-over), 0x00c71e59 CALL 0x00b3d2a0 (no argument, bare RET), 0x00c71e60 CALL 0x00ba9370 (one stack argument, RET 0x4), and 0x00c71e56 CALL EDX, the register-indirect table slot.

observed_mechanics: 0x00c71e30 56 - PUSH ESI: the prologue. It exists because 0x00c71e31 writes ESI and ESI is callee-saved on i386, NOT because the receiver needs to cross a call in ESI - the receiver's survival across 0x00c71e3d is 0x00b8dab0's obligation to leave ESI alone, which it does in seven bytes.
0x00c71e31 8b f1 - MOV ESI,ECX: ModRM 0xf1 is mod=11, reg=110 (ESI), rm=001 (ECX). The receiver is aliased into ESI and no register is saved here - the save is the PUSH above.

0x00c71e33 8b 8e 3c 01 00 00 - MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x13c]: ModRM 0x8e is mod=10 (disp32 follows), reg=001 (ECX), rm=110 (ESI); the disp32 is 0x0000013c. Base and destination DIFFER, so the incoming receiver is consumed and the LOADED WORD IS NOW IN ECX, in place of it. Opcode 0x8b, so a LOAD and not a LEA.
0x00c71e39 85 c9 - TEST ECX,ECX: writes EFLAGS only, and its ModRM is reg=ECX rm=ECX, so the flags come from the word 0x00c71e33 LOADED, not from the incoming receiver.

0x00c71e3d e8 6e bc f1 ff - CALL 0x00b8dab0: rel32 0xfff1bc6e is -933778, and 0x00c71e3d + 5 + that = 0x00b8dab0. NOTHING between 0x00c71e33 and here writes ECX (0x00c71e39 and 0x00c71e3b write EFLAGS only), so this is a RECEIVER HAND-OVER: 0x00b8dab0's own ECX IS the word at receiver+0x13c.

0x00b8dab0, read live: 8b 81 94 01 00 00 c3 = MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x194] / RET. Its ModRM 0x81 is rm=001 (ECX), so it reads through the register the hand-over left holding the loaded word, and its seven bytes name no register but EAX - which is why ESI survives the call and the receiver can still be read at 0x00c71e47.

0x00c71e42 83 f8 05 - CMP EAX,imm8 = 5: opcode 0x83 is the sign-extending imm8 form, so this compares all thirty-two bits of EAX against +5; 0x3d would be imm32 and 0x80 a byte-wide compare, and neither occurs. The value compared is therefore the 32-bit word at (word at receiver+0x13c) + 0x194 - a word of the DELEGATED object, not of this body's receiver.

0x00c71e45 75 20 - JNZ rel8 = +32: 0x00c71e47 + 2 + 32 = 0x00c71e67. BOTH branch operands name the SAME address, so the body has exactly two returns and not three, and the null arm is one arm reached two ways.

0x00c71e47 8b 86 d4 00 00 00 - MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI + 0xd4]: ModRM 0x86 is mod=10, reg=000 (EAX), rm=110 (ESI); the disp32 is 0x000000d4. Opcode 0x8b, so a LOAD - the word at +0xd4 is the TABLE POINTER, and EAX now holds an address.

0x00c71e4d 8b 50 4c - MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x4c]: ModRM 0x50 is mod=01, so the displacement is a single disp8 byte and that byte is 0x4c; reg=010 (EDX), rm=000 (EAX). 0x4c is 76, which is nineteen four-byte words. Note the operand-class change from the previous instruction (mod=10 disp32) to mod=01 disp8: 0x4c really is one byte here, not the low half of a larger displacement.

0x00c71e50 8d 8e d4 00 00 00 - LEA ECX,[ESI + 0xd4]: THE OPCODE IS 0x8d where 0x00c71e47's was 0x8b, over the SAME displacement. That is the load/address distinction, and it is decidable in this body because one instruction dereferences the address and the next forms it. So the dispatch's receiver is the ADDRESS of the embedded object - not the table pointer stored there, and not this body's own receiver.

0x00c71e56 ff d2 - CALL EDX: ModRM 0xd2 is mod=11, so the target is a REGISTER and there is no displacement operand here to be mistaken for the slot offset; 0x4c was consumed by 0x00c71e4d and is not seen again. The only indirect transfer in the body, and the derived dispatch record counts exactly one.
0x00c71e58 50 - PUSH EAX: one dword, the value the dispatch returned.
0x00c71e59 e8 42 b4 ec ff - CALL 0x00b3d2a0: rel32 0xffecb442 gives 0x00c71e59 + 5 + (-1262014) = 0x00b3d2a0.

0x00b3d2a0, read live: SIX bytes, `a1 e4 ea 67 01 c3` = MOV EAX,moffs32 [0x0167eae4] / RET. The opcode 0xa1 is the moffs form and carries NO ModRM byte at all, so there is no register field a receiver could have arrived in and none a stack argument could have been read through: this callee takes NOTHING. Its RET is the bare 0xc3, so it pops NOTHING either - which is what leaves the word pushed at 0x00c71e58 alive. 0x0167eae4 is that function's data address and is named nowhere in this package.

0x00c71e5e 8b c8 - MOV ECX,EAX: ModRM 0xc8 is mod=11, reg=001 (ECX), rm=000 (EAX). ECX is OVERWRITTEN with the previous call's result, so the last call's receiver is 0x00b3d2a0's result and nothing about ECX has to survive the call at 0x00c71e59.

0x00ba9370, read live, is what makes the pushed word's fate decidable: 0x00ba9370 PUSH ECX, then 0x00ba9371 `83 7c 24 08 ff` CMP dword ptr [ESP+0x8],-0x1. At that point [ESP+0x8] IS [ESP+4] of the callee's own ENTRY frame - the PUSH ECX having moved the return address from [ESP] to [ESP+4] - so it is the word 0x00c71e58 pushed, and that word is this callee's ONE stack argument. BOTH of its returns are `RET 0x4` (0x00ba93a1 on the found path, 0x00ba93a8 on the not-found path), so the CALLEE pops it.

0x00c71e65 5e - POP ESI therefore restores the CALLER'S ESI, the word saved by the PUSH at 0x00c71e30 - and NOT the word pushed at 0x00c71e58, which 0x00ba9370's `RET 0x4` has already taken. A POP cannot reach below a word a callee's RET consumed. The in-binary corroboration is 0x00ba9370 itself, which writes ESI at 0x00ba9377 and so does the identical PUSH ESI (0x00ba9376) / POP ESI (0x00ba939f) for the identical reason, while also ending in `RET 0x4`: one listing, both facts, and the two mechanisms visibly doing different work.
0x00c71e66 c3 - RET: bare, no imm16, so the entry pops nothing and the caller owns cleanup.

0x00c71e67 33 c0 - XOR EAX,EAX: ModRM 0xc0 is mod=11, reg=000, rm=000, EAX both sides, so all thirty-two bits of EAX are written with zero. Not the 8-bit `30 c0` and not `33 c8` (XOR EAX,ECX, which would leave EAX dependent on ECX).
0x00c71e69 5e / 0x00c71e6a c3 - POP ESI / RET: the second exit, restoring ESI the same way.

The body is 59 bytes, 0x00c71e30..0x00c71e6a, matching the live ghidra_function record's body_span_bytes: 59 and body_end: "00c71e6a". The `PUSH ESI`/`POP ESI` pair is the i386 callee-saved contract for ESI, required because 0x00c71e31 WRITES ESI. It is NOT a mechanism for carrying the receiver across a call, and the derived record's `saved_registers: [ESI]` corroborates the reading. The receiver's survival across 0x00c71e3d is 0x00b8dab0's obligation to leave ESI alone, which its seven bytes do.

0x00c71e3d is a receiver HAND-OVER, proved by the chain of ECX: 0x00c71e33 overwrites ECX with the loaded word and nothing between it and the call writes ECX, so 0x00b8dab0 receives that word as its own receiver and `CMP EAX,0x5` compares (word at receiver+0x13c) + 0x194 against 5.
Both branch operands name 0x00c71e67, so the body has exactly two returns and the null arm is one arm reached two ways. That is why `XOR EAX,EAX` appears once.

0x00c71e47 and 0x00c71e50 use the SAME displacement with opcodes 0x8b and 0x8d, so the load/address distinction is decidable inside this one body: the table pointer is LOADED and the embedded object's ADDRESS is FORMED.

The word pushed at 0x00c71e58 is the LAST callee's argument, not the previous call's: 0x00b3d2a0 takes nothing and pops nothing (opcode 0xa1 has no ModRM byte; its RET is the bare 0xc3), and 0x00ba9370 reads that word on entry and both of its exits are `RET 0x4`. `POP ESI` at 0x00c71e65 therefore restores the CALLER's ESI.
0x00c71e5e overwrites ECX with 0x00b3d2a0's result, so the last callee's receiver is that result and nothing has to survive the preceding call.

the delegation is a receiver hand-over and the compared value belongs to the DELEGATED object at +0x194: 0x194 is shown to be past this body's own receiver extent, and the two objects are shown to be non-mergeable

the table word is LOADED and the dispatch's receiver is its ADDRESS: the callee reports the receiver it was handed, and it is shown to differ from the stored table pointer, from the live table, from the trap table and from this body's own receiver; the 0x8b/0x8d pair over one displacement is pinned

the slot is the word at table+0x4c and a wrong index is OBSERVABLE: every word from +0x40 to +0x5c is a distinct callable slot and a callable sentinel sits immediately past +0x5c, so a one-, two-, three- or four-slot error calls a different function that says so, one further lands on the trap, and one inside the prefix cannot land on a valid pointer. The model test drives all eight neighbours through the ONE accessor the entry uses

the pushed word reaches the LAST callee and is popped by that callee's `RET 0x4`, while `POP ESI` restores the CALLER's ESI: ESP is sampled before the call and after the return and must agree on both paths; the two cleanup facts are pinned as DIFFERENT; changing only the dispatch's result moves the last call's ARGUMENT and changing only the global slot's result moves the last call's RECEIVER, so neither is a constant and neither is the outer receiver

the return crosses verbatim on the passing arm and is a full 32-bit zero on the null arm: 8 interesting values and a 4x4 byte sweep cross unchanged, `33 c0` is pinned as a 32-bit XOR rather than the 8-bit or ECX-relative forms, and the two arms are told apart even when the last call returns zero

the encoding is the observed 59 bytes and the reach is bounded: every ModRM field, opcode, disp8/disp32, rel8 and rel32 is decoded and tied by static_assert to the header's constants, the branch and call addresses are recomputed from the encoded operands rather than restated, and the record's own words (verdict, completeness, both candidate conventions, one indirect call, zero vtable-shaped loads, one saved register, two receiver displacements) are pinned with the disagreement included

focused_test.harness_note: Two harness properties are load-bearing and were both found by measurement, not by taste. `check` is __attribute__((noinline)): with it inlinable, at -O2 on both compilers, the optimizer folded the ESP balance comparison against samples whose storage it had reallocated around the assembly block, and a green reconstruction failed. And the lookup's observation channel is read through a volatile-qualified lvalue, because a `memory` clobber does not order a plain global read against it and one compiler folded a routing assertion onto the PREVIOUS call's observation. Copying inside the assembly block was tried first and is worse: the compiler may allocate an ordinary "r" input to EAX, which the call has just overwritten.

focused_test.mutation_summary: 61 distinct mutants were applied: 44 source-level and 17 encoding/constant-level. 60 of 61 are DETECTED - every source-level mutant except one, and all 17 encoding-level mutants - and the one survivor is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT, reported as equivalent rather than counted as a gap: M32 adds an unused volatile sink, a dead store that changes no observable behaviour on any input. Its nearest non-equivalent relative, M35b (call the slot twice and keep the second result), is killed, so the dead-store blind spot is closed rather than excused. Breakdown by group: wrong 0x13c (2), wrong 0xd4 on each of its two levels (6), wrong slot displacement at 0x44/0x48/0x50/0x58/0x60 (5), wrong compare constant 4 or 6 (2), inverted second guard (1), inverted/dropped first guard (2), inverted or dropped second guard (2), void-expression guard (1), LEA-vs-MOV confusion at the dispatch receiver (2), pushed-word routing into the wrong callee (2), skipped global-slot call (1), slot not called (1), double-called slot (1), wrong return on the passing arm (2), wrong return on each null arm (3), dropped guard sites (2), perturbed delegated scalar (1), perturbed delegation target (1), perturbed lookup result (1), zeroed global-slot result (1), observation channel falsified (2), wrong lookup receiver (1), dropped pushed word (1), perturbed pushed word (1), statically-false guard (1); plus 10 header-constant/layout mutants and 7 encoding-byte mutants, every one of which trips a static_assert at compile time.
focused_test.mutation_method: Each mutation is a single textual replacement applied to a fresh copy of the package under /tmp/opencode/mut/w - never to the staging files - built with g++ -m32 -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra and run. A mutation counts as detected when the binary aborts (exit 134), faults (exit 139), or fails to compile. Replacements that matched zero or more than one site were re-anchored until unique, and the two LEA-vs-MOV mutants were first rejected as compile errors for a const-correctness reason rather than for a semantic one, so they were rewritten to compile and were then killed by value. The unmutated baseline was rebuilt and re-run after the battery and passes all six compiler/optimisation configurations.

The 61st is M32, the dead-store perturbation, which is deliberately NOT in the table because it SURVIVED and is reported as an equivalent mutant in mutation_summary instead - an enumerated 'expected FAILS' row it did not meet would be a false claim.

blocker.detail: the return register EAX is written at a width the dimension cannot bound on at least one of the 2 reachable return(s) in the complete 21-instruction listing
blocker.cause: the last definition of EAX before the RET at 0x00c71e66 is the CALL at 0x00c71e60. The dimension treats a call result as an unbounded width by construction, and says why: on x86-32 whether a caller may read EAX after a call is decided by the CALLEE's signature, which this listing cannot show.
blocker.why_it_is_a_machine_ceiling: Nothing in the reconstruction can change it. The machine writes EAX on the passing arm only through that call - 0x00c71e65 is POP ESI and 0x00c71e66 is RET, neither touches EAX - so there is no width-bearing EAX write to bound, and there is no second machine source for that width inside this VA's listing. Removing the call or adding an EAX write would each be a claim the bytes refute.
blocker.the_fact_that_is_true_but_outside_this_d: 0x00ba9370 DOES establish 32 bits, from its own listing read live: its only writes to EAX are `33 c0` (XOR EAX,EAX) at 0x00ba93a4 and `8b 40 14` (MOV EAX,[EAX+0x14]) at 0x00ba939c, both full 32-bit, and both of its exits are `RET 0x4`. So the modelled 32-bit width is CORRECT and is recorded as observed in this package. It is a fact about a DIFFERENT function's listing, and the dimension deliberately does not read other VAs' listings - it declines to invent a second oracle. This package therefore states the 32-bit width on the evidence of 0x00ba9370's own bytes and does not pretend the dimension granted it.
blocker.not_done: No validator arm was weakened, no tooling was edited, no evidence was manufactured, and no runtime PASS was asserted. The runtime axis is GATED, which is correct and expected.
